text: {"question":"How does the treatment of peculiar‑velocity uncertainties in the Hubble‑flow subset of the Pantheon+ sample influence the inferred value of the Hubble constant compared with the full sample that includes Cepheid‑calibrated hosts?","reference_answer":"When the analysis restricts to supernovae with redshifts above 0.05, the peculiar‑velocity contribution to the distance‑modulus error drops to about 0.035 mag, making it negligible relative to the typical 0.1 mag scatter. This high‑redshift cut yields an H0 of 72.9 ± 0.9 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, only 0.4 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ lower than the Pantheon+ value and still 6 σ above the CMB‑derived ΛCDM result, demonstrating that the elevated H0 persists even after removing the most velocity‑sensitive supernovae.","passage_1_contribution":"Passage A quantifies how peculiar‑velocity errors diminish with redshift and shows that a z > 0.05 cut leaves H0 essentially unchanged, indicating the high H0 is not driven by velocity uncertainties.","passage_2_contribution":"Passage B describes the full Pantheon+ dataset, including Cepheid‑calibrated hosts, and the statistical framework used to compute distance‑modulus residuals and χ², providing the baseline H0 against which the high‑redshift subset is compared.","joint_reason":"Both passages together allow one to assess the impact of peculiar‑velocity corrections on the H0 determination by comparing the high‑redshift, velocity‑insensitive subset (Passage A) with the full sample that incorporates Cepheid calibration (Passage B).","same_quantity":true}
